name: Margo Hurries Down the Stairs
description: Margo descends the staircase quickly, her steps coming faster as she moves downward.
related_events: Margo hurries down the staircase

name: Margo Remembers the Unease Before the Party
description: The applause lingers in the air. Margo settles back into her chair, her fingers working at a loose edge of fingernail polish. A quiet moment passes. She remembers the hours before Bill's welcoming-home-birthday party, the way the air had felt heavy, how she had sensed something was about to go wrong.
related_events: Margo recalls sensing disaster before the party began
Margo sits back in her chair and picks at her fingernail polish

name: Margo Catches Eve in the Dress
description: Margo enters and looks around for Eve. She spots Eve near the wings, standing before two cheval mirrors with Margo's dress held up against her body. Eve turns from side to side, then bows as if acknowledging applause, imitating Margo's mannerisms. Margo watches quietly, a look of curiosity on her face, then smiles. She calls out, 'Eve.' Startled, Eve drops the gown and turns toward her. Margo speaks softly, 'I think we'd better let Mrs. Brown pick up the wardrobe.' Without a word, Eve picks up the dress and brings it over to Margo.
related_events: Margo discovers Eve imitating her in costume
Eve tries on Margo's dress and mimics her performance
Margo instructs Eve to return the dress to Mrs. Brown
Eve silently returns the dress to Margo

name: Margo and Karen Share a Silent Toast
description: Amid steady applause at the party, Margo twirled her highball glass and caught Karen's gaze. She lifted her glass in a quiet toast. Karen offered a faint smile in return, but it soon faded as her eyes drifted thoughtfully toward Eve.
related_events: Margo raises glass in silent toast to Karen
Karen responds with wan smile to Margo's toast
related_occasions: Party Margo Gave For Bill'S Return From Hollywood

name: Drive to the Station
description: Lloyd and Karen drove through the snowy countryside in Lloyd's car. Margo sat with them as they made their way to the train station late on Monday afternoon. The cold weekend had passed, and by now Margo and Lloyd were speaking to each other again, their earlier distance softened into civility.
related_events: Lloyd and Karen drive Margo to the station
Margo and Lloyd become civil after emotional distance
Lloyd drives car through snowy countryside

name: Margo Remembers the Time Eve Became Her Anchor
description: Margo runs her fingers along the side of her nearly empty highball glass, lost in thought. She declines the whiskey Addison offers, her gaze drifting down to the glass before lifting to look at Eve. In that moment, she remembers how Eve had felt like home the first time they met, how her room reminded her of Wisconsin. Over the next three weeks, Eve was beside her constantly—guiding her, caring for her, defending her. She was there in every way, becoming sister, lawyer, mother, friend, psychiatrist, and cop all at once.
related_events: Margo reflects on her past experience with Eve

name: Margo Declines Addison's Whiskey
description: Margo runs her fingers up and down the sides of her nearly empty highball glass. Addison watches her for a moment, then offers her the whiskey. Margo shakes her head without looking at him, her gaze fixed on the glass. She sets it down and lifts her eyes toward Eve.
related_events: Margo declines Addison's offer of whiskey

name: Karen Joins Margo for Lunch at '21'
description: A cab pulls up to the restaurant '21'. Karen steps out, pays the driver, and goes inside. She meets Margo, and the two sit down together for lunch, wearing hats, chatting like old friends.
related_events: Cab arrives at restaurant '21'
Karen exits cab and enters restaurant
Margo and Karen have lunch at '21'
related_occasions: Lunch Meeting At '21' Between Karen And Margo

name: Karen and Eve Arrive at the Theater
description: Karen and Eve enter the theater. Karen greets the doorman, saying, 'Good evening, Gus,' and begins walking toward Margo's dressing room. Eve lingers behind, taking in the surroundings. She says, 'You can breathe it - can't you? Like some magic perfume...' Karen smiles, takes Eve's arm, and they continue down the hall together.
related_events: Karen greets the doorman upon arrival
Karen leads Eve toward Margo's dressing room
Eve expresses awe at the theater environment
Karen takes Eve's arm and continues to Margo's dressing room

name: Margo Interrupts Bill and Eve's Conversation
description: Margo reaches the landing and walks casually toward the living room. Inside, Bill and Eve are laughing together as Bill finishes a story. Eve chuckles at his words, then notices Margo approaching and stands up. Bill turns around as Margo enters the room.

Margo walks casually toward the living room

Bill turns around upon Margo's arrival

name: Karen Wakes and Lights a Cigarette
description: Karen sits up in bed, unable to sleep. She lights a cigarette and stares into the dark room. The phone rings suddenly, startling her. It also wakes Lloyd, who stirs in bed. Karen picks up the phone and says, 'Hello... who?... who's calling Mr. Richards?'
related_events: Karen wakes up and lights a cigarette
Karen reflects on her feelings of helplessness in her marriage

name: Phone Call in the Night
description: The phone rings suddenly, cutting through the stillness of the room. Karen, already awake, reaches for it and lights a cigarette. The sound stirs Lloyd, pulling him from sleep. She answers, her voice quiet. 'Hello... who?... who's calling Mr. Richards?'
related_events: Phone rings and startles Karen, waking Lloyd
Karen answers the phone and responds to an unknown caller

name: Margo Arrives at the Theater
description: Margo steps out of a cab in front of the theater on a Friday afternoon. The building is quiet, no performance scheduled. She goes inside. As she moves through the empty space, she recalls a saying: 'This, too, will pass away.' Two weeks later, it is the day of the audition, and things are well between Bill and her, and between her and the world.
related_events: Margo exits cab and enters theater
Margo reflects on wise man's saying

name: Margo and Bill Reunite Before the Audition
description: Two weeks after Margo visited the theater on a quiet Friday afternoon, she arrives again on the day of the audition. The air between her and Bill is easy, their relationship restored. They move together as if the distance between them had never formed, sharing quiet moments and familiar glances before she steps inside to prepare.
related_events: Bill and Margo reconcile before audition

name: Karen and Eve Hesitate Before Entering Miss Channing's Room
description: Karen and Eve walk toward a closed door marked with a typed chit that reads MISS CHANNING, the paint on the door peeling. As they near, a loud, uninhibited guffaw from Margo comes through the door, causing them to stop. Karen whispers to Eve, telling her to wait a moment, and smiles. Eve responds with a shaky smile. At that instant, Margo's voice rings out from inside, saying, "Honey chile," I said, "if the South had won the war, you could write the same plays about the North!" Karen steps into the room as the voice continues.
related_events: Karen and Eve approach Miss Channing's closed door
Margo's loud guffaw causes Karen and Eve to pause
Karen whispers to Eve to wait a moment

name: Karen Enters as Margo Speaks
description: Margo's voice carries through the closed door, delivering a sharp, mocking remark about the Civil War. As she speaks, Karen opens the door and steps inside, entering the room while Margo's words are still in the air.
related_events: Margo delivers a sarcastic remark about the South winning the war
Karen enters the room while Margo is speaking

name: Addison Arrives and Listens at Margo's Dressing Room Door
description: After the performance ends, Addison enters the theater and makes his way toward Margo's dressing room. The door is slightly ajar. He stops beside it and listens. From inside, Bill's voice can be heard saying, 'You were better than all right, kid, you gave a performance, you rang a bell.' Holding his cane, Addison pushes the door open wider and steps into view.
related_events: Addison enters the theater after the performance ends
Addison pauses to listen at Margo's dressing room door
related_occasions: Post-Performance Gathering Near Margo'S Dressing Room

name: Addison Opens the Door with His Cane
description: Addison stands beside the slightly open dressing room door, having overheard voices from within. He lifts his cane and uses it to push the door open wider, revealing the room more fully. The motion allows him—and the observer—to see and hear clearly what is happening inside.
related_events: Addison uses his cane to open the dressing room door
related_occasions: Post-Performance Gathering Near Margo'S Dressing Room

name: Margo and Birdie Finalize Party Preparations
description: Margo stands at her dressing table, finishing her jewelry before the party. She takes a sip from a large martini. Birdie enters the room and zips up the back of Margo’s dress. Margo asks if the extra help has arrived. Birdie replies that a group of people dressed as maids and butlers has shown up, making a remark about their questionable appearance. Margo responds with a dry comment about hiring actors. Birdie then says the caterer had to go back for hors d'oeuvres. Margo laughs and makes a joke about a French ventriloquist, and Birdie replies that he taught her everything. As Birdie begins tidying the room, she mentions a message from the bartender—domestic gin was ordered by mistake. Margo quips that the only mistake was inviting the guests, adding they won’t care as long as the drink burns. She asks where Bill is, noting he’s late. Birdie says he’s already been there for twenty minutes. Margo expresses surprise that he hasn’t come up to see her.
related_events: Margo puts on jewelry before the party
Birdie assists Margo with her dress zipper
Margo inquires about the extra help arrival
Birdie reports on the caterer's delay with hors d'oeuvres
Birdie delivers message about domestic gin order mistake

name: Margo Wonders Where Bill Is
description: Margo stands at her dressing table, finishing her jewelry and sipping a large martini. She asks Birdie where Bill is, remarking that he’s late for the party. Birdie zips up Margo’s dress and replies that Bill has already been there for twenty minutes. Margo expresses surprise, saying she finds it odd he hasn’t come up to see her.
related_events: Margo comments on guest selection and domestic drinks
Birdie confirms Bill's arrival at the party

name: Addison Walks Eve to Her Room
description: Addison walks with Eve down the corridor toward her room. They talk about the time, and Eve remarks there is still plenty of time for a nap, saying they rehearsed most of the previous night. Addison suggests she could sleep too. When they reach her door, Eve opens it. Addison comments on her ability to rest before a performance, calling her a killer, then correcting himself to say champion, joking that he mixes up his boxing terms. As he turns to leave, Eve calls his name and invites him inside for a moment, saying she has something to tell him. Addison pauses, then steps in after her.
related_events: Addison and Eve walk to Eve's door
Eve opens her door

name: Addison's Farewell and Correction at Eve's Door
description: Addison and Eve arrive at her door. He tells her it's almost four, and she remarks there's still time for a nap since they rehearsed most of the night. Addison suggests she could sleep too. He says, 'The mark of a true killer,' and offers a handshake, adding, 'Sleep tight, rest easy—and come out fighting.' Eve asks why he called her a killer. Addison pauses, then replies that he meant champion, not killer, and explains he sometimes mixes up his boxing terms. He turns and begins to walk away. After a few steps, Eve calls his name. He stops. She invites him in for a minute, saying she has something to tell him. Addison turns back and follows her inside.
related_events: Addison mislabels Eve as a killer then corrects to champion

name: Eve Calls Addison Back and Invites Him Inside
description: As Addison turned to leave, Eve called out to him. He paused. She asked him to come in for a minute, saying she had something to tell him. Addison turned back, entered the room, and followed her inside.
related_events: Eve invites Addison into her room
Addison enters Eve's room after invitation

name: Karen Arrives at the Theater Alley
description: Karen's taxi pulls up to the alley behind the theater shortly after the final curtain. Through the rain-speckled window, she tells the driver to wait. She opens the door, steps out onto the wet pavement, and closes the door behind her. The marquee above the theater entrance still glows faintly, advertising 'Aged in Wood' with 'Max Fabian Presents' and 'By Lloyd Richards' beneath. Other nearby theaters are darkening their lights. Karen pauses, looks around, then walks toward the alley entrance.
related_events: Karen's taxi arrives at the theater alley
Karen instructs the taxi driver to wait
Karen exits the taxi

name: Karen Waits and Looks for the Girl
description: Karen steps out of the taxi and pauses, glancing around the quiet street. The rain drizzles lightly as theater lights dim around her. She turns her gaze toward the alley, then hesitates, searching the sidewalk as if expecting someone. Her expression softens with a faint, wistful smile. After a moment, she lowers her head and walks into the alley.
related_events: Karen hesitates and looks about curiously before entering the alley
Karen reflects on her habit of seeing the girl at the theater

name: Karen Enters the Alley After the Show
description: Karen smiles faintly, then lowers her head and walks into the alley.
related_events: Karen smiles at her own romanticism and heads into the alley

name: Margo Reads Addison's Column
description: Margo strides around the room, reading excerpts from Addison's column aloud. She mocks the flowery language, then grows increasingly agitated as she reads passages criticizing mature actresses and hinting at her own fading relevance. Karen sits quietly, expressing shock that Eve would allow such things to be written about her. Margo skips ahead, finds another section, and reads aloud accusations about older actresses clinging to youth and blocking younger talent. Karen whispers that she can't believe Eve said those things. Margo crumples the newspaper in her hands and hurls it across the room.
related_events: Margo reads Addison's column aloud with growing anger
Karen expresses disbelief at Eve's betrayal
Margo crumples the newspaper in fury

name: Margo Confronts the Betrayal
description: Margo paces the room, clutching Addison's column, her voice rising as she reads aloud excerpts that criticize her and praise Eve. She crumples the newspaper in her hands, her anger directed at Eve and Addison, accusing them of spreading lies. She declares that someone must have gone to great lengths to ensure critics attended that performance. Vowing not to let it stand, she says she will force Eve into Addison’s throat if no one else takes action. Bill enters, having rushed over after reading the column, and finds Margo overcome. She turns away, then collapses into his arms, silent, as he holds her. Karen watches, then quietly leaves the room.
related_events: Margo accuses Addison and Eve of orchestrating a smear campaign
Margo threatens to take violent revenge on Eve and Addison

name: Bill Arrives and Comforts Margo
description: Bill bursts into Margo's living room, having just read Addison's column. He is breathless from rushing there. Margo, overcome with emotion, turns away and begins to cry. Bill takes her in his arms, holding her tightly as she leans into him. He speaks softly, telling her he is there and that everything will be all right. Karen, still in the room, looks at them and quietly remarks on her being out of place. Bill offers a small smile in response. Karen returns the smile, gives a brief wave, and leaves the room.
related_events: Bill arrives at Margo's living room after reading Addison's column
Bill comforts Margo as she cries in his arms
Karen acknowledges her presence as unnecessary in the intimate moment
Karen exits the living room after exchanging a smile with Bill

name: Addison Observes After Eve's Performance
description: The snow is shoveled to either side of the alley, leaving a narrow lane. Addison stands with his back to the camera, facing the stage door. A few actors pass by, leaving the theater after the performance. He begins to walk toward the door. The sound of the audience's loud, enthusiastic applause lingers in the air. Some members of the audience had chosen to return later to see Margo perform, but those who stayed applauded Eve vigorously and at length. Addison recalls the phone call from Eve inviting him earlier that afternoon, and how several newspaper representatives happened to be in attendance as well, all invited to see the understudy's performance.
related_events: Addison reflects on Eve's performance
Eve receives loud and sustained applause
Audience members express preference for Margo's performance

name: Eve's Invitation to the Understudy Performance
description: The snow had been shoveled to either side of the alley, leaving a narrow lane. Addison stood with his back to the street, facing the stage door. A few actors passed by, leaving the theater after the performance. Addison began to walk toward the door. Earlier that day, Eve had called and invited him to attend the afternoon understudy performance. He arrived to find several representatives from other newspapers already there. The audience had thinned, many choosing to return another time to see Margo, but those who stayed responded enthusiastically to Eve, cheering loudly and at length.
related_events: Eve invites Addison to attend the performance
Addison mentions the presence of newspaper representatives at the performance

name: Addison Leaves After the Performance
description: The final curtain falls at the theater. Snow is piled to either side of the alley, leaving a narrow path. Actors emerge from the stage door, stepping out into the cold. Addison stands with his back to the alley, facing the door. He begins to walk toward it, joining the quiet dispersal of the night's performers and guests.
related_events: Performance concludes at the theater

name: Waiting at the Baggage Counter
description: Margo, Eve, and Bill stand in line at the American Airlines baggage counter, behind a few couples waiting to check in. The rain has stopped, but the ground is wet. Margo's arm is linked through Bill's as they wait. A passenger ahead speaks earnestly with the dispatcher, holding up the line. Bill watches, then sighs. Margo remarks that the airline times things so passengers board at the last minute, just so they can close the doors and leave. When the passenger finally moves on, Eve suggests she handle the check-in while Margo and Bill spend a moment together. Bill agrees and hands Eve the ticket. Margo smiles at her, and Eve smiles back before stepping forward to check in.
related_events: Margo, Eve, and Bill wait behind couples at baggage counter
Margo becomes aware of imminent separation from Bill
Eve senses her emotional superfluity in the moment
Bill observes passenger speaking with dispatcher
Bill sighs while waiting in line
Margo comments on airline boarding timing

name: Eve Takes the Ticket
description: At the American Airlines baggage counter, Margo, Eve, and Bill wait behind several couples in line. The air is damp from recent rain. Margo's arm is linked through Bill's as they stand together, aware of the approaching separation. Eve watches quietly. When the passenger ahead moves away from the counter, Bill starts forward, but Eve speaks up. She suggests that she handle the check-in while Margo and Bill take a moment together before the flight. Bill agrees and hands her the ticket. Margo turns to Eve and smiles, her thanks unspoken. Eve returns the smile, then steps up to the counter as Margo and Bill move aside.
related_events: Eve proposes to handle check-in while Margo and Bill spend time together
Bill hands Eve the airline ticket
Margo expresses gratitude to Eve with a smile
Eve smiles in response to Margo's gratitude

name: Eve and Margo Exchange Letters and Script
description: Eve arranges a stack of letters at the desk and carries them to Margo, who is seated by the fire with a play script. Margo shakes her head and holds her nose, then hands the script to Eve. Eve smiles and offers the letters in exchange. Margo takes the letters, preparing to sign them.
related_events: Eve arranges stack of letters and carries them to Margo
Margo rejects script by shaking head and holding nose
Eve smiles and exchanges script for letters with Margo

name: Birdie Serves Tea and Eve Takes the Call
description: Birdie enters the room carrying a tea tray and sets it down on the low table in front of the fire. As she arranges the cups, the phone rings. Birdie and Eve both move toward it, but Eve reaches the phone first. She speaks into the receiver with polite firmness, declining something or turning someone away. Birdie glares at Eve, then at Margo, who remains seated by the fire, eyes closed, head tilted back. After the call, Eve returns to Margo, handing her a stack of letters to sign. Birdie picks up the tea tray and exits, slamming the double doors behind her.
related_events: Birdie brings tea tray and sets it by the fire
Phone rings and Eve answers it before Birdie
Eve gives someone a polite but firm refusal on the phone

name: Birdie's Exit After Eve Takes the Call
description: After Eve finishes the phone call, Birdie glares at her, then turns her gaze toward Margo. Margo leans her head back and closes her eyes, resting quietly by the fire. Without a word, Birdie strides to the double doors, pulls them open, and slams them shut behind her as she leaves the room.
related_events: Birdie glares at Eve and then at Margo
Margo reclines with eyes closed in apparent relief
Birdie exits forcefully, slamming the door

name: Margo Questions Birdie About Eve
description: Margo, propped up in bed, sips her orange juice and asks Birdie if she likes Eve. Birdie replies that she’d rather give an answer than get into an argument, and says no. Margo presses her, listing Eve’s qualities—hardworking, loyal, efficient. Birdie responds dryly that Eve works night and day, and is as devoted as an agent with only one client. Margo insists Eve thinks only for her, but Birdie hesitates before saying Eve thinks only about her, as if studying her like a play, a book, or a set of blueprints—how she walks, talks, thinks, eats, sleeps. Margo cuts in sharply, saying it sounds flattering and surely nothing is wrong with that. Just then, Eve enters in a smart suit, asking what they think of it. Margo says it looks better on Eve than it did on her. Eve offers to return the suit, but Margo declines, calling it too 'Seventeenish.' Eve confirms she has the script for the Guild and the tax checks. As she turns to leave, Margo asks if Eve made a midnight call to Bill for his birthday. Eve gasps, admitting she forgot to tell Margo—she meant to say something before Margo went out, but must have been asleep when she returned. She adds that she sent Bill a telegram herself. Eve exits. Margo stares at the closed door, then at Birdie. Birdie leaves without a word. Alone, Margo looks down at her orange juice and slowly twirls it in the shaved ice.
related_events: Margo questions Birdie about her opinion of Eve
Birdie compares Eve's attention to studying a blueprint
Margo reacts defensively to Birdie's comparison

name: Eve's Visit with the Portfolio
description: Eve entered Margo's bedroom carrying a leather portfolio. She greeted Margo, who returned the greeting, while Birdie remained silent. Eve showed off her new suit, altered from one of Margo's, and asked for an opinion. Margo said it looked better on Eve but was too youthful for her own taste. Eve laughed and said she had already taken care of Margo's errands—the script was ready to return to the Guild, and the tax checks were with her. Margo remarked that Eve had thought of everything. As Eve turned to leave, Margo asked if she had placed a call to Bill at midnight California time. Eve gasped, remembering she had forgotten to tell Margo. She explained she had meant to mention it before Margo went out with the Richards but must have fallen asleep. Margo acknowledged the oversight quietly. Eve added that she had sent Mr. Sampson a telegram for his birthday, knowing how important he was. She smiled shyly and left. Margo stared at the closed door, then at Birdie, who said nothing and walked out. Margo sat alone, swirling her orange juice in the glass.

Eve displays her new suit to Margo and Birdie

Margo acknowledges Eve's thoroughness

name: Margo Stares After Eve's Exit
description: After Eve leaves the room, Margo remains still, her eyes fixed on the closed door. She then turns her gaze to Birdie, who stands quietly by. Without speaking, Birdie turns and walks out, leaving Margo alone. Margo looks down at her glass of orange juice, slowly swirling it in the bed of shaved ice.
related_events: Margo reacts silently to Eve's absence
Birdie leaves the bedroom without speaking
Margo absently plays with her orange juice

name: Karen Meets Eve at the Stage Door
description: Karen walks toward the stage door and passes a recess in the wall. A soft voice calls out—Eve's—stopping her. Karen looks, hesitates, then sees Eve barely visible in the shadows. Eve steps forward into the light of a gooseneck lamp above them, revealing her face and simple clothes: a cheap trench coat, low-heeled shoes, a rain hat perched on the back of her head. Her large eyes seem to glow in the dim light. Karen smiles and greets her, remarking that it felt odd not seeing her there. Eve asks why she wouldn't be, and Karen responds with mild surprise, noting how often Eve must have been watching. They speak briefly, and Karen takes Eve's arm, insisting on introducing her to Margo. Eve resists, but Karen leads her toward the door, asking her name. Eve says, 'Eve Harrington.' Karen opens the door, and they go in together.
related_events: Karen approaches the stage door and notices a recess in the wall
Eve speaks to Karen from the shadows of the recess
Eve emerges from the recess under the gooseneck light
Karen greets Eve and expresses surprise at her consistent presence

name: Karen and Eve's Conversation by the Stage Door
description: Karen walks toward the stage door and notices a recess in the wall. Eve’s voice softly calls out, 'Mrs. Richards...' Karen pauses and sees Eve barely visible in the shadows. Eve steps forward into the dim light from a gooseneck lamp above. She wears a cheap trench coat, low-heeled shoes, and a rain hat perched at the back of her head. Her large eyes catch the light as she looks up at Karen. Karen smiles and waits. Eve approaches. Karen says, 'So there you are. It seemed odd, suddenly, your not being there...' Eve asks why she wouldn’t be. Karen replies that after weeks of seeing Margo enter and leave the theater six nights a week, it might seem unusual to expect Eve to still be there. Eve says she hoped it wasn’t a problem that she spoke. Karen assures her it isn’t. Eve admits she’s seen Karen often and that it took all the courage she could muster to say anything. Karen smiles and says it must be strange to approach just a playwright’s wife, calling herself the lowest form of celebrity. Eve responds that Karen is Margo Channing’s best friend and that she and her husband are always with Margo and Mr. Sampson. She asks what he’s like. Karen grins and says Bill Sampson is a director. Eve says he’s the best. Karen replies that he’ll agree with her. She then asks Eve what she does between the times Margo goes in and comes out. Eve says she sees the play. Karen looks surprised and asks if she’s seen every performance. Eve nods. Karen asks if she finds it expensive. Eve says standing room doesn’t cost much and that she manages. Karen studies her, then takes her arm and says she’s going to introduce her to Margo. Eve hesitates, pulling back slightly, saying she’d be imposing and would just be another fan gushing. Karen insists there isn’t anyone like her and begins guiding her toward the stage door. Eve says she didn’t know, maybe another time, implying she isn’t dressed properly. Karen tells her she looks fine. At the door, Karen asks her name. Eve says, 'Eve. Eve Harrington.' Karen opens the door, and they go in together.

Karen downplays her own significance as a playwright's wife
Eve expresses admiration for Bill Sampson's directorial talent
Karen inquires about Eve's activities during Margo Channing's performances

Eve steps out of the shadows, wearing a cheap trench coat, low-heeled shoes, and a rain hat perched on the back of her head. The dim light catches her large, luminous eyes. Karen smiles and greets her. Eve explains she has been attending every performance from standing room, though it takes effort to manage the cost. Karen is surprised but touched. She takes Eve's arm and insists on introducing her to Margo Channing. Eve resists, saying she would feel like an intrusive, tongue-tied fan. Karen reassures her, saying she looks fine, and gently leads her to the stage door. As they reach it, Karen asks for her name. Eve tells her: Eve Harrington. Karen opens the door, and they go inside together.

name: Karen and Eve Enter the Theater

name: Addison and Eve Walk to the Taft Hotel on Opening Night
description: Addison and Eve stand in front of the theater, looking at Eve's photo on the lobby display. The marquee announces a new play by Lloyd Richards, presented by Max Fabian, opening that night. Addison remarks that to the theater world, New Haven is just a stretch of sidewalk between the Shubert Theater and the Taft Hotel. They begin walking toward the hotel, Eve's arm through Addison's. She calls it a heavenly day. Addison calls it D-day. Eve grins and says she thought she would be panic-stricken, but instead, she cannot wait for the night to come. Addison asks if she is sure of tomorrow, and she replies, 'Aren't you?' He says he is. Eve says the night will bring her everything she has ever wanted, marking the end of an old road and the beginning of a new one. Addison asks what the new road is paved with, and she answers, 'Stars.' She goes inside the hotel, and Addison follows.

Addison asks what the new road is paved with. Eve replies, 'Stars.' She smiles and goes inside, with Addison following behind.

name: Eve and Addison Enter the Taft Hotel

name: Addison Confronts Eve About Her Lies
description: Addison confronts Eve in a corner of the room, demanding answers. He accuses her of being a liar, pointing out that she was paid to leave town. Eve throws herself onto the bed, face down, and begins to cry. Addison moves closer, relentless. He tells her there was no Eddie, no pilot, and that she has never been married—that claiming otherwise dishonors real heroes and the women who loved them. Eve sobs and covers her ears; Addison pulls her hands away. He continues, revealing that San Francisco has no Shubert Theater and that she has never been to North Shore or San Francisco, calling the lie careless and beneath her. Eve turns to look at him, tears streaming down her face, and says she had to say something, be someone, to get Margo to like her. Addison replies that Margo did like her, helped her, trusted her, and that Eve repaid her by trying to take Bill away. Eve denies it, but Addison insists he saw and heard her through the dressing room door. He accuses her of using his name and his column to pressure Karen into giving her the role of Cora, and of lying to him about it. Eve mumbles into the bed that it isn’t true. Addison says he had lunch with Karen just hours ago and that she revealed more than she learned. He asks if Eve wants to change her story about Lloyd banging on her door the other night. Eve covers her face and pleads with him to stop. Addison steps off the bed and looks down at her. He says it now seems impossible that he could ever want her, but perhaps that is exactly why—they are both improbable. He lists what they share: a contempt for humanity, an inability to love or be loved, ambition, and talent. He says they deserve each other and asks if she is listening. Eve lies still, her cheek against the bed, and nods. He demands she speak. She says yes, Addison. He asks if she understands that she belongs to him completely. She says yes, Addison. He tells her to take a nap and wishes her good luck for tonight. As he turns to leave, Eve says in a flat voice that she won’t play tonight, that she can’t, she couldn’t go on. Addison pauses, smiles, and tells her she will give the performance of her life. He exits. The camera stays on Eve’s face, tear-stained and still. Her eyes close, and she falls asleep.

He corrects her—‘the Theatuh’—and challenges her narrow view, asking who decided theater only exists in certain cities or buildings. It’s all theater, he says, wherever there’s magic, make-believe, and an audience. He tells her not to approve or disapprove—just accept that theater is for everyone, even if it’s not her kind. Eve says she only asked a simple question. Bill grins and admits he talked too much, blaming the ‘bushwah’ in the so-called Ivory Green Room. He lies down again. name: Addison and Bill Debate the Nature of Theater People
description: Karen and Birdie come down the stairs to join Bill, Max, Addison, and Miss Caswell, who are seated on the steps. Birdie continues down to the first floor while Karen stays behind. Addison begins speaking, claiming that actors and actresses are nothing like ordinary people, and that their appeal lies in their very difference from normal human beings. He says that theater folk in New York, Hollywood, and London are made up of neurotics, egomaniacs, and emotional misfits, and that these traits are what make them artists. Miss Caswell, watching Birdie pass with her sables, remarks that such fur is something a girl might make sacrifices for. Bill mutters in response that she probably has. Miss Caswell says she meant sable, not Gable. Max asks if she meant Clark Gable, and she replies that either one works. Addison continues, insisting that theatrical people are a breed apart, displaced personalities unlike the rest of humanity. Bill laughs and tells Eve she won’t need to read Addison’s column the next day, since she’s just heard it, but says he doesn’t agree. Addison replies that disagreement is Bill’s particular abnormality. Bill admits there are eccentric people in the theater, but says they stand out because of the spotlight and fanfare, not because they represent the norm. He argues that the theater is mostly hard work—built on sweat, effort, and skill. He adds that to be good in the theater, one must want it more than anything else, requiring intense ambition, desire, and sacrifice. Eve suddenly says, 'Yes. Yes, it does.' Bill goes on, saying such dedication means the people who pursue it can’t be ordinary. Max interrupts, asking what makes a man become a producer. Addison answers by comparing a producer to a man who walks into a lion cage with only a chair. Max says that answer satisfies him completely. Miss Caswell calls out to a passing butler, 'Oh, waiter,' but he ignores her. Addison tells her that’s not a waiter, it’s a butler. She says she can’t very well shout 'Oh, butler,' in case someone’s name is Butler. Addison concedes she has a point, though an idiotic one. She says she just wants a drink. Max gets up and offers to get it for her. She thanks him, and he leaves with her empty glass. Addison remarks to Bill that Max’s career is rising in the East like the sun, then asks what Bill was saying.
